proposals.title: Integrated Tissue Domain Detection using Spatially Informed Latent Embedding
proposals.summary:
This proposal focuses on delineating tissue organization by integrating gene expression and spatial coordinate data into a unified latent space. The analysis begins with rigorous quality control and the construction of a multi-scale spatial neighborhood graph that preserves local tissue architecture. Clustering methods are then applied to identify distinct tissue domains, with subsequent differential expression analysis to validate domain-specific markers.

Evaluation will involve quantitative metrics comparing spatial coherence and transcriptional variation, ensuring that the resulting latent representation accurately reflects both molecular profiles and anatomical structure. Expected outcomes include clear visualization of tissue boundaries and enhanced biological insight into tissue organization.

proposals.title: Spatial-Driven Visualization and Embedding for Multi-scale Tissue Architecture
proposals.summary:
This analysis emphasizes the creation of spatially aware embeddings that facilitate intuitive, interactive visualization of tissue architecture across varying scales of resolution. The workflow integrates gene expression profiles with spatial coordinates using weighted joint dimensionality reduction techniques. A central component is the development of robust, interactive visual dashboards that map latent space dynamics directly to tissue morphology.

The approach is designed to clearly reveal spatial gradients and local variations within the tissue. Validation comes from comparing the spatial coherence of embeddings with known histological or annotated tissue structures, aiming to improve interpretation and exploration of complex spatial-omics datasets.

proposals.title: Trajectory and Gradient Modeling with Spatial Contextualization
proposals.summary:
This proposal is built around the inference of biological trajectories and gradients within spatial transcriptomics data. By incorporating spatially-informed latent representations, the analysis models continuous biological states and transitions that underpin tissue development or disease progression. The method leverages conditional trajectory inference techniques that are adjusted to account for spatial neighborhood structures.

The pipeline begins with quality control and the construction of spatial graphs, followed by dimensionality reduction and trajectory mapping. Evaluation will focus on the consistency of inferred biological gradients with known developmental or pathological processes, as well as the integration of spatial context to enhance gradient interpretation.

proposals.title: Batch-Aware Spatial Transcriptomics: Harmonizing Replicates via Spatial Regularization
proposals.summary:
Addressing a critical gap in current spatial omics analyses, this proposal focuses on integrating and harmonizing data from multiple batches or replicates while preserving spatial coherence. The analysis introduces methods to adjust for batch effects by incorporating spatial regularization into the latent space construction. By aligning spatial graphs across replicates and applying batch-corrected dimensionality reduction, the pipeline ensures that biological variation is preserved while technical variability is minimized.

The proposal outlines rigorous testing using cross-replicate consistency metrics and evaluation of spatial neighborhood preservation. The expected outcome is a robust framework that improves the comparability of multi-sample data and enhances the overall biological signal in spatial transcriptomics datasets.

proposals.title: Spatially Constrained Denoising and Smoothing for Robust Expression Recovery
proposals.summary:
This analysis proposes a spatially informed denoising framework specifically designed to recover true gene expression signals in the presence of technical noise and dropout. The approach combines traditional imputation methods with spatial smoothing techniques that respect local tissue boundaries. A spatially-aware latent representation is computed first, allowing for the execution of targeted dropout recovery using synthetic dropout simulations and spatial constraint penalties.

Evaluation metrics will include recovery accuracy against known expression benchmarks and spatial consistency checks. The framework is anticipated to improve the clarity of expression profiles, thereby enhancing downstream analyses such as domain detection and differential expression assessment.

proposals.title: Expression Reconstruction and Cross-Modality Integration in Spatial Context
proposals.summary:
Focusing on the challenge of reconstructing and integrating gene expression data with additional omics modalities, this proposal leverages spatial context to enhance reconstruction accuracy. The analysis integrates multi-modal data sources by constructing a joint latent space that respects both the spatial organization of tissues and molecular interdependencies across modalities. This enables effective imputation of missing signals as well as cross-modality correlation analyses.

The pipeline will be validated using benchmark metrics for expression reconstruction accuracy and consistency of spatial mapping across modalities. The outcome is expected to provide a comprehensive view of cellular states within their native spatial context, thereby facilitating deeper insights into tissue function and heterogeneity.

proposals.title: Robust Spatial Latent Integration with Multi-scale Neighborhood and Dropout Recovery
proposals.summary:
This proposal aims to develop a computational approach that integrates multi-scale spatial neighborhood information with gene expression data to build a robust latent representation. The framework employs a fusion of spatially informed dimensionality reduction and explicit dropout recovery techniques, including synthetic dropout simulations and spatial autocorrelation adjustments during differential expression analysis.

The analysis is structured to rigorously evaluate how well local and global spatial features are preserved, using both clustering performance and recovery of transcript expression as validation metrics. Anticipated outputs include a latent space that not only reveals discrete tissue domains but also captures subtle gradients in expression, thus bridging the gap between expression recovery and spatial domain delineation.

proposals.title: Modular Integrated Analysis Pipeline for Spatial Omics: Balancing Domain Detection, Gradient Inference, and Reconstruction
proposals.summary:
This comprehensive proposal presents a modular analysis pipeline designed to cater to multiple facets of spatial omics data, including domain detection, gradient inference, and expression reconstruction. The approach is structured into distinct modules that interlink: one focused on creating a spatially informed latent space for domain detection, another on modeling continuous biological gradients, and a third on reconstructing expression signals with spatial context.

Each module includes rigorous quality control, construction of multi-scale spatial graphs, and the use of tailored dimensionality reduction techniques. The pipeline is designed for flexibility, allowing for targeted evaluation of each component using domain-specific metrics and visualization strategies. Overall, this integrated framework is expected to offer a balanced, robust solution for comprehensive spatial omics analysis that can be adapted to diverse datasets and experimental conditions.

plan.user_request: Coordinate domain agents to produce and refine exactly eight computational spatial-omics analysis proposals, resulting in a final JSON file of proposals without executing any analyses.

steps.title: Draft eight spatial analysis proposals
steps.description: Use the Spatial-CV Planning Agent (`spatial_cv_agent`) to design a set of eight candidate computational spatial-omics analyses grounded in the provided background on spatially aware latent representations. The agent will write these as a valid JSON draft to `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json`, describing plausible analyses (but not running them) that evaluate or exploit spatially informed representations for tasks such as tissue organization and expression reconstruction.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated spatial CV planning agent is best suited to interpret the latent-representation-focused background and propose analyses most likely performed in the hidden paper. This step creates the initial structured hypothesis space as a machine-readable draft file that subsequent critique and synthesis steps can refine.
steps.assignment_rationale: Step 1 must be handled by the Spatial-CV Planning Agent, which is explicitly designed to draft exactly eight spatial analysis proposals and write the audited draft to hypotheses/draft_proposals.json.

steps.title: Critique draft proposal set
steps.description: Use the Critic agent to read `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and generate a structured critique of the eight proposed analyses, assessing plausibility, redundancy, coverage of key goals (domain detection, visualization, trajectory/batch handling, denoising, expression recovery), and alignment with the constraints of spatial transcriptomics. The Critic will write its evaluation and recommendations to `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json`.
steps.reasoning: A separate critique phase identifies gaps, overlaps, and inconsistencies in the draft proposals and checks how well they match the paper’s implied aims, without altering the original draft. Producing a standalone critique artifact makes the feedback explicit so the final synthesis step can systematically improve titles and summaries while preserving eight distinct, well-justified analyses.
steps.assignment_rationale: The Critic Agent is the only specialist whose advertised role is to read draft proposals and produce a structured critique artifact at hypotheses/critique.json, matching this step’s required output.

steps.title: Synthesize final proposal set
steps.description: Use a synthesis-oriented hypothesis agent (e.g., the Hypothesis agent with its final-synthesis capability) to combine `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json` into a refined set of exactly eight computational spatial-omics analysis proposals. The agent will rewrite and, if needed, minimally adjust the proposals for coherence and coverage while not executing any analysis, and will output `project/outputs/hypotheses/final_proposals.json` as a JSON object whose only top-level key is `proposals`, mapped to an array of exactly eight items; each item will contain only `title` and a detailed `summary` describing a single proposed analysis.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated synthesis step is needed to transform the critiqued draft into a clean, final proposal set that strictly adheres to the required schema and cardinality. By explicitly consuming both the draft and critique artifacts, this step ensures that the final eight proposals are internally consistent, well-motivated by the spatial representation background, and encoded in the precise JSON format requested.
steps.assignment_rationale: The Hypothesis Agent is the synthesis-oriented planner that advertises writing final proposal files, making it the appropriate agent to consume the draft and critique and emit the final hypotheses/final_proposals.json.

provenance.justification: Existing templates (e.g., for hypothesis testing or paper-driven hypothesis generation) define multi-step workflows with different structures and goals than the user’s strict three-step, file-specific proposal pipeline. To respect the requirement of exactly three compact steps and the mandated artifact paths and agents, this plan was written from scratch without applying a template.
